findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

On arrival, no CFPM is available at the facility. PIC stated that the CFPM (Anthony Emery) was running errands and should return soon. By the end of the inspection, a CFPM was still not available at the facility. PIC instructed to ensure that enough CFPMs are available for all times food handling operations are taking place.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1) 4-203.12: (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be accurate to +/- 1.5C. (B) accurate to +/- 3 Fahrenheit.  

The ambiant air temperature measuring device in the meat room is not accurate. The thermometer shows an air temperature of 45F while inspector’s instruments indicate a temperature of 33F. PIC placed a new independent thermometer into the cooler to correct. 


4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. 

The walk in cooler for the meat room does not have a temperature measuring device inside. PIC supplied a thermometer during the inspection to correct.

Cases of raw beef (ribs) and chicken are observed stored on the floor in the walk in cooler used for prepping items for smoking. PIC was consulted and the items moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

When asked about food handler certifications for the employee in the meat room today, the PIC checked and then stated that they did not have a food handlers certification. PIC is instructed to ensure that the food handlers have an up-to-date food handler certification. Inspector will check again at the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

1) Hams in the island display cooler closest to the entryway nearest the cardboard compactor are observed with varying temperatures (34F-58F). Investigation showed that any items above the vents are out of temperature (46F-58F observed). PICV was instructed to ensure that items in the cooler are left flat to the bottom of the cooler to ensure that the temperatures are maintained correctly. Employee only placed items in the cooler recently and they are being allowed to bring them back to temperature. 2) Chicken in the angled display cooler as customers are entering the facility are observed with varying temperatures. PIC was consulted and individual items probed to find where the coolers safe plain for cold holding was located. PIC was unaware of the last time the cooler was stocked and two containers of chicken tenders were discarded as being to warm (46F and 47F observed internal temperatures). All other items were observed in correct temperatures.

PIC is instructed to ensure that the building is maintained in a state of good repair.
